title: Dynamic curve
slide_intent: Teach designers to reserve a predictable place for the mark. A clear boundary lets the reader distinguish the organization from the photograph or headline beside it.
strategic_value: Special Olympics can link publications from different programs through a recurring arc that echoes the circular symbol. Its edge gives the mark a separate field even when the surrounding content varies.
demonstration: A montage places the arc on a handbook, athletic photographs, banners and program marks. Three notes describe its circular origin, available formats and selective use on covers, posters and flyers.
practical_value: Choose a prominent surface that needs the curve to house the mark. The examples show where the device adds recognition and the notes explain why an inside brochure page can omit it.

content_islands.name: Page heading
content_islands.spec: Set Visual identity in gray at left and Dynamic curve in red at the head of the main column.

content_islands.name: Usage notes
content_islands.spec: Stack three illustrated notes in the left margin. Address the circle, the prepared formats and the surfaces that warrant the curve.

content_islands.name: Purpose statement
content_islands.spec: Place a bold paragraph above the examples. Explain how the curved field separates the mark from competing elements.

content_islands.name: Application montage
content_islands.spec: Overlap the handbook, covers and banners in the lower main field. Keep the red-and-white curve visible at different scales and align the standing pieces to a common baseline.
